newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up despite mild temps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up despite mild temps.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were unchanged to slightly higher Friday in sluggish trade, with stable crude and some exports, particularly high sulphur to Mexico, underpinning the complex, market sources said.

"Until we get some heat, I don't see prices moving up much more, but the Mexicans have bought seven cargoes (of high sulphur) and they may be looking for more," said one trader, adding hotter weather was needed to stir some utility load.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent remained talked at $16.50-75 a barrel, with June and July paper also steady in the $16.60-16.80 area, traders said.
They said forecasts next week for more mild East Coast weather offered little hope for improved generation demand near-term.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally firmed slightly to about $17.25.
High sulphurs in New York also scored gains, with 2.2 percent up 25-50 cents to near the $15 level, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable but well-supported, with one percent still at $16.25 and three percent at $14.25-50.
Traders said two 45,000-barrel high sulphur pieces (FOB Port Arthur) sold late Thursday at $13.85 (specs unavailable) and $14.60 (2.8 percent, 12 API).

June gas prices at the New York city gate slipped about five cents Friday to the $2.45/mmBtu area, or $15.44 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, fell by more than a nickel to $2.23/mmBtu, or $14.05 a barrel.
